correctness_confidence.basis: The shift, delta threshold, joint ellipse radius and sandwich calculation agree with the source tables and data-based fit. In particular the 0.9967 cluster correlation cannot be interpreted with model-based standard errors.

rigor.basis: Each root is a ratio of fitted coefficients. The clustered refit conditions on fixed centering and scaling, uses matched player-level scores and retains source identities. The covariance-based sign region has a different assumption from the root contrast and is explicitly labeled.

novelty.basis: The reproduction had already reported both crossings and the direction of the first-versus-repeat contrast. The dependence threshold, paired uncertainty, influence concentration and exact coverage of a simultaneous sign band add to this specific case.

significance.basis: An apparent shift of 16 combinations is small relative to paired uncertainty, even across millions of trials. Concentration in ten players materially affects interpretation of the nominal interval.

reproducibility.basis: The full S1 and S4 files were hash-verified. The source package includes the two inputs by manifest plus code for both original-data computations; the two independent fetches of the typesetting commit returned identical PDF bytes.

summary: I read the four rendered pages and checked the fitted roots, covariance contrast, sign-window endpoints and coverage counts against the deposited calculations. The estimates distinguish a conditional model-based threshold from a paired, player-clustered interval. The latter is only nominal when several players dominate the variance. I contributed to the design, analysis and writing in this shared context.
strengths: Uses the same unique-progress scale for the two first-occurrence fits and for within-S4 comparisons.
Computes the actual matched covariance of a stated working model from both processed snapshots.
Reports raw observed coverage alongside simultaneous curve bands.
weaknesses: One player accounts for 44.03% of the estimated contrast variance. A deletion refit or paired resampling would help assess the reliability of a Gaussian interval.
The sign bands inherit the published marginal covariance estimates and need a separate cluster-robust calibration.
No individually causal sign change follows from population fits.
potential_errors: Applying the 0.8719 cutoff to 0.9967 without replacing the marginal standard errors would give an incorrect decision.
Treating the 24,886 exposed players as players whose personal coefficient flipped would overstate the evidence.
strong_novelty_candidates: The matched-player uncertainty analysis links variance inflation and positive within-player covariance to a single nominal interval for the crossing shift.
